'''Wilfred Allen Subritzky''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|QSM|size=85%}} (20 November 1925 – 23 December 2015) was a New Zealand lawyer and property developer, active from the mid-1950s until the mid-1980s. His company, Universal Homes, mass-produced houses in standard designs, and sold 14,000 houses over the 30-year period of Subritzky's involvement.<ref>" The Cutting Edge : The Bill Subritzky Story " p 98.</ref><ref>[http://www.doveministries.com/content/prominent-lawyer-developer-and-evangelist-bill-subritzky-dies-age-90 "Prominent lawyer, developer and evangelist Bill Subritzky dies age 90"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009163439/http://www.doveministries.com/content/prominent-lawyer-developer-and-evangelist-bill-subritzky-dies-age-90 |date=2016-10-09 }} (retrieved October 6, 2016)</ref>

==Biography==
Subritzky was born in 1925, and lived in [[Auckland]]. In 1971 he became involved in the [[charismatic movement]], and became an independent evangelist and healer. Subritzky's [[faith healing]] ministry, Dove Ministries, distributes pamphlets, books and videos of his teaching and his evangelistic healing meetings. He was a charismatic [[Anglican]] but the style of his ministry was more similar to [[Pentecostal]]s such as the late [[Derek Prince]].<ref>{{cite news  | last = Shaw| first = Bob| title = Evangelist plans to make Good Word his last word| publisher = The Evening Post| date = June 29, 1998| url = http://www.lexisnexis.com.remote.slc.edu/lnacui2api/results/docview/docview.do?docLinkInd=true&risb=21_T12248011812&format=GNBFI&sort=RELEVANCE&startDocNo=1&resultsUrlKey=29_T12248011815&cisb=22_T12248011814&treeMax=true&treeWidth=0&csi=155910&docNo=2| accessdate = June 30, 2011}}</ref>

Subritzky was a proponent of the [[Toronto Blessing]] and its introduction into New Zealand.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z7l4O-i_80sC&dq=%22Subritzky%22+%22Toronto+Blessing%22&pg=PA67|title=Fathers Blessing: A Refreshing Move of God That Is Shaking Toronto-And the World|first1=John G|last1=Arnott|first2=James|last2=Arnott|page=67|year=1996|publisher=Charismatic Media|isbn=9780884194040 }}</ref> He frequently attributed problems, whether physical, spiritual, emotional or psychological, to the influence of [[demon]]s, which he claimed to "cast out".<ref>{{cite news  | last = Brown| first = Andrew| title = Evangelist can find a demon for every ill| newspaper = The Independent| date = September 15, 1990| url = http://www.lexisnexis.com.remote.slc.edu/lnacui2api/results/docview/docview.do?docLinkInd=true&risb=21_T12248011812&format=GNBFI&sort=RELEVANCE&startDocNo=1&resultsUrlKey=29_T12248011815&cisb=22_T12248011814&treeMax=true&treeWidth=0&csi=8200&docNo=3| accessdate = June 30, 2011}}</ref> He also claimed to have insight through the "[[word of knowledge]]" into people's sins, which have made them vulnerable to demonic influence.<ref>{{cite news  | last = Brown| first = Andrew| title = Evangelist delivers demon warning| newspaper = The Independent| date = February 14, 1990| url = http://www.lexisnexis.com.remote.slc.edu/lnacui2api/results/docview/docview.do?docLinkInd=true&risb=21_T12247918801&format=GNBFI&sort=RELEVANCE&startDocNo=1&resultsUrlKey=29_T12247918804&cisb=22_T12247918803&treeMax=true&treeWidth=0&csi=8200&docNo=5
| accessdate = June 30, 2011}}</ref> Skeptics questioned his claim that he had ability to cure ailments such as asthma, arthritis and cancer, stating that he used [[psychological manipulation]] to make people feel as though they were healed.<ref>{{cite news  | title = Sceptics question faith healing | publisher = [[Television New Zealand]] | date = 2006-10-24 | url = http://tvnz.co.nz/view/page/411419/868561 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news  | last = Crewdson| first = Patrick| title = Exorcism exercise for fired-up faithful | pages =  3| publisher =  The Dominion Post | date = May 21, 2007| url = http://www.lexisnexis.com.remote.slc.edu/lnacui2api/results/docview/docview.do?docLinkInd=true&risb=21_T12248011812&format=GNBFI&sort=RELEVANCE&startDocNo=1&resultsUrlKey=29_T12248011815&cisb=22_T12248011814&treeMax=true&treeWidth=0&csi=256380&docNo=10| accessdate = June 30, 2011}}</ref>

Subritzky was a friend to the controversial Nigerian "prophet" [[T.B. Joshua]] and publicly supported him amidst criticism that Joshua's "miracles" were not of God.<ref>{{cite news  | last = Egwugum| first = Jackson| title = T.B. Joshua Divides Western Christians | publisher = Charisma Magazine | date = June 30, 2002| url = http://www.charismamag.com/site-archives/218-peopleevents/news/646-tb-joshua-divides-western-christians}}</ref>

In 1986, Subritzky and other conservative Christians helped establish the [[Coalition of Concerned Citizens]], a right-wing Christian pressure group formed to oppose the socially-liberal policies of the [[Fourth Labour Government]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Jesson|first1=Bruce |author-link1=Bruce Jesson |first2=Allanah |last2=Ryan|author-link3=Paul Spoonley|first3=Paul |last3=Spoonley |title=Revival of the Right: New Zealand Politics in the 1980s |edition=1st |publisher=Heinemann Reed |year=1988 |pages=56 |chapter=Chapter 4: Remoralising Politics |isbn=0-7900-0003-2}}</ref>  He was married to Lucy Patricia (Pat), who died in 2011. Subritzky later married Kaylene.

In the [[1991 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|1991 New Year Honours]], Subritzky was awarded the [[Queen's Service Medal]] for community service.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=52383 |date=31 December 1990 |page=31 |supp=2}}</ref>

Subritzky published his autobiography ''On the Cutting Edge: The Bill Subritzky Story'' in 1993.<ref>Published by Sovereign World Ltd (Kent, UK) {{ISBN|1 85240 107 9}} PB; {{ISBN|1 85240 131 1}} HB.</ref>

In 2014, Subritzky's {{convert|8.9|ha|acre|0|abbr=on}} estate in [[Lynfield, New Zealand|Lynfield]], Mount Roskill was sold to [[Ryman Healthcare]] with an estimated market value of $16.2 million. The property was developed by Subritzky and his first wife, Pat, in 1960 and featured several homes, a pool, tennis court, sheds and a separate office wing from where Subritzky ran his businesses.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-07-21|title=Ryman buys central Auckland Subritzky estate|url=https://www.nbr.co.nz/article/ryman-buys-central-auckland-subritzky-estate-dl-159508|access-date=2020-08-14|website=NBR|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Gibson|first=Anne|date=2016-09-07|title=Ryman's plans for 600-resident Auckland retirement village|language=en-NZ|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/news/article.cfm?c_id=3&objectid=11705220|access-date=2020-08-14|issn=1170-0777}}</ref>

Subritzky died on 23 December 2015.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wilfred Allen (Bill) Subritzky |url=http://notices.nzherald.co.nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/obituary.aspx?n=wilfred-allen-subritzky-bill&pid=177021622 |accessdate=26 December 2015 | newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>

==Honorific eponyms==

Subritzky Avenue in [[Mount Roskill]] was named after him.<ref name="Roskill">{{citeq|Q116775081|page=159}}</ref>
